title: Sunny Finds a Feather | Bedtime Story
description: Sweet little Sunny the quokka discovers a beautiful blue-and-white feather on the path and wonders about the kookaburra who left it behind. A gentle, dreamy story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories that will drift little ones softly off to sleep.
narration:
Late in the afternoon, when the bush was quiet and golden, Sunny the quokka was padding slowly along her favourite path through the trees.

And there, right in the middle of the path, was a feather.

She stopped and looked at it for a long moment. It was beautiful — long and striped in blue and white, with soft brown edges. She had never seen a feather quite like it.

She picked it up very carefully in her small paws and turned it over and over. It was lighter than she expected. Lighter than almost anything.

She looked up at the sky, trying to imagine the bird who had dropped it. A kookaburra, she decided. A big, kind kookaburra with bright eyes, who had flown through these very trees and left this small gift behind without knowing it.

Sunny sat down on a warm flat rock and held the feather up so it caught the last light. The bush was going quiet around her — the cicadas settling, the breeze slowing, everything growing still.

And then, from somewhere far away in the trees, she heard it. A soft, rolling kookaburra laugh — not loud, just a gentle, sleepy sound, like the bush saying goodnight.

Sunny smiled. She tucked the feather carefully beside her and curled up on the warm rock. The sky above the treetops deepened from gold to soft purple, and the stars were just beginning to think about appearing.

She closed her eyes, still smiling, still holding the feather close.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little blue feather. Goodnight, little one.
